brief: A volatile week featured heavy hedge fund de-grossing. Prime brokerage data for 22 October showed the 5th largest de-grossing event this year, driven entirely by long selling, the largest long selling since September 2025. Net leverage keeps falling even as gross exposure stays elevated, hedge fund allocation to semiconductors and semi equipment has dropped substantially, and the US momentum factor has given back all of this year's gains, with cyclicals versus defensives weakening in the same move. Separately, the capex super-cycle is intensifying competition for capital as interest rates stay higher, so tech is no longer capital-light: US hyperscalers' operating cash flow is becoming insufficient to fund capex, increasing reliance on external financing, though leverage in both US and European tech remains low versus the broader market. A 100bp increase in the cost of debt would cut STOXX 600 earnings by 3%. Europe's interest expense as a share of sales and net debt to EBITDA are both rising, and refinancing rates have sat above the coupons on already-issued debt since 2022. On earnings, 3Q surprises ran slightly below the historical average, but analysts still expect 24% H2 EPS growth for the STOXX 600, or 15% excluding commodities.
